Create one documentary photograph that tests a legendary-scale five-finger grip trace as measurable physical site evidence on a storm-cleared moor, with the supplied image guiding only the visible adult researcher's facial, hair, and makeup appearance.

A layered medium-wide documentary photograph at blue hour after rain on a windswept coastal moor. One unmistakably adult woman works as a field researcher beside a storm-wet, salt-worn boulder. A single enormous hand-shaped trace occupies one exposed rock face. One broad palm hollow connects continuously to five separate finger grooves. The five grooves vary in length and spread naturally from the same palm. Their crushed, salt-paled mineral edges interrupt the darker weathered rock skin. The researcher holds a rigid measuring scale directly across the palm hollow, while numbered evidence markers follow all five fingertip ends. Her face remains legible: long near-black wavy hair with a center part and soft face-framing strands, brown almond-shaped eyes, softly defined straight brows, fine dark eyeliner, luminous warm-neutral skin, and muted rosy lips. Cold mist layers behind her and the boulder, and raking twilight reveals the trace as documented material evidence within the landscape.
